absent: Locking, concurrency, and ordering rules for these ioctl payloads.
Error codes, permission checks, and master and capability enforcement.
Kernel side implementation of contexts, drawables, blank waits, port memory, GEM, prime, syncobj, mode setting, and leases.
Structure padding, alignment, and 32 bit compatibility beyond implied field widths.
Event delivery, descriptor lifetime, fence signaling internals, and timeout and deadline handling.

findings.text: A direct memory access exchange descriptor identifies a rendering context and separates outbound and inbound buffer work. It records how many buffers to send with user pointers to handle and length lists for that direction, carries a flag set, then records how many buffers are requested with a desired size plus user pointers to index and size lists, and finally reports how many buffers were granted.

A context record pairs a handle with a flag set where preserved and two dimensional only are the defined bits. A context result vector pairs a count with a user pointer to an array of context records so size and storage are separated. A drawable record is a thin wrapper around a drawable handle.

Drawable information defines a clip rectangles query kind. An update draw request carries a drawable handle, a type selector, an element count, and an opaque data token able to hold a user address. An authentication record carries only a magic token used to prove client identity.

An interrupt routing record identifies a device location with four integers for interrupt line, bus number, device number, and function number, allowing user space to associate an interrupt with a specific slot.

Absolute wait kind is zero and relative is one. High controller selection uses mask 0x3e. Event is 0x4000000, flip is 0x8000000, next on miss is 0x10000000, secondary is 0x20000000, signal is 0x40000000. High controller shift is one. Types mask combines absolute and relative. Flags mask combines event, signal, secondary and next on miss.

A blank wait request carries a sequence type, a sequence number, and a signal token. The reply carries a sequence type, a sequence number, and a time split into seconds and microseconds. A union overlays request and reply so one payload serves both directions.
Pre modeset notification value is one and post modeset notification value is two.

A modeset control pairs a display controller identifier with a command selector. An AGP mode record carries one mode value. An AGP buffer record carries size, handle, memory type and a physical hint with size rounded to page granularity. An AGP binding pairs a buffer handle with a page rounded byte offset. AGP info reports version major and minor, mode, aperture base and size, allowed and used memory, plus vendor and device identifiers. A scatter gather record carries page rounded size and handle. A version record carries interface major and minor plus driver major and minor.

Memory object management uses small fixed records. Close carries a handle plus padding. Flink exports a handle to a global name. Open maps a name back to a handle and reports object size in sixty four bits. Change handle carries an old handle and a replacement handle.

Device capability numbers are dumb buffer 1, blank high controller 2, dumb preferred depth 3, dumb prefer shadow 4, prime 5, timestamp monotonic 6, async page flip 7, cursor width 8, cursor height 9, addfb2 modifiers 16, page flip target 17, controller in blank event 18, syncobj 19, syncobj timeline 20, atomic async page flip 21.
Prime capability bits are import one and export two, indicating directional buffer sharing support.
Capability query and client capability setting share the same shape of two sixty four bit fields for capability identifier and value, giving a uniform get and set protocol.
Client capability numbers are stereo 3D one, universal planes two, atomic three, aspect ratio four, writeback connectors five, cursor plane hotspot six, plane color pipeline seven.
Device open mode aliases the read write flag and the close on exec flag from process open flags.
A prime handle exchange carries a buffer handle, a flag field meaningful for handle to file conversion, and a signed file descriptor for the exported or imported buffer.

Synchronization object creation reports a handle and accepts flags, while destruction takes a handle plus padding. A file handle exchange record carries handle, flags, file descriptor, padding, and a sixty four bit timeline point. A transfer record carries source and destination handles with source and destination points plus flags and padding.

Create signaled is bit zero. File to handle import sync file is bit zero and timeline is bit one. Handle to file export sync file is bit zero and timeline is bit one. Wait all is bit zero, wait for submit bit one, wait available bit two, wait deadline bit three. Query last submitted is bit zero.

Blocking waits carry a user pointer to handles, an absolute timeout in nanoseconds, a handle count, flags, an index of first signaled valid unless waiting for all, padding, and a monotonic deadline hint. Timeline wait adds a user pointer to points for per handle targets. Eventfd association carries handle, flags, point, file descriptor and padding. Array forms carry a user pointer plus count, with timeline array adding a points pointer and flags.

Controller sequence query carries a controller identifier and returns active state, most recent blank sequence, and a nanosecond timestamp of first pixel out. Queue sequence carries controller identifier, flags, a sequence field used as target on input and actual on output, and opaque user data. Client name setting carries a length and a user pointer to name bytes.
Relative sequence flag is one and next on miss is two. Maximum client name length is sixty four.
Ioctl base magic is the character d. Four wrappers provide no payload, read, write, and read write directions built on that base.

Base numbered entries zero through eight cover version exchange, unique identifier exchange, magic retrieval, interrupt bus routing, map, client, statistics, version selection, and modeset control, with read, write, or bidirectional direction per entry.

Memory and capability entries cover memory close 0x09, flink 0x0a, open 0x0b, capability query 0x0c, client capability setting 0x0d, prime handle to file 0x2d and file to handle 0x2e, second generation framebuffer query 0xCE, framebuffer close 0xD0, client name setting 0xD1, and handle replacement 0xD2.

Legacy entries 0x10 through 0x2c cover unique setting, magic authentication, blocking control, map and buffer management, shared area context mapping, master acquire and release, context add through result enumeration, drawable add and remove, direct memory access, and lock, unlock and finish operations, each with the direction encoded in its wrapper.

Graphics port entries 0x30 through 0x37 cover acquire, release, enable, info, alloc, free, bind and unbind. Scatter gather entries 0x38 and 0x39 cover alloc and free. Entry 0x3a waits for blank, 0x3b and 0x3c query and queue controller sequences, and 0x3f updates drawables.

Mode setting entries 0xA0 through 0xB1 cover resources, controller get and set, cursor, gamma get and set, encoder, connector, deprecated attach and detach, property get and set, blob get, framebuffer get and add, framebuffer remove, page flip, and dirty framebuffer.

Extended mode entries 0xB2 through 0xBE cover dumb create, map and destroy, plane resources, plane get and set, second generation framebuffer add, object property query and set, second cursor, atomic commit, and blob create and destroy. Lease entries 0xC6 through 0xC9 cover create, list lessees, get and revoke.

Synchronization entries 0xBF through 0xC5 cover create, destroy, handle to file, file to handle, wait, reset and signal. Timeline entries 0xCA through 0xCD cover timeline wait, query, transfer and timeline signal. Entry 0xCF binds an event file descriptor.
Driver specific command numbers range from hexadecimal forty inclusive to hexadecimal A0 exclusive.

Every event begins with a type and length header. A blank event adds user data, seconds, microseconds, sequence, and controller identifier where zero means unsupported on older kernels. A controller sequence event adds user data, a signed nanosecond timestamp, and a sequence number.
Event types are blank one, flip complete two, and controller sequence three.

Capability get and set use identical identifier value width so queries and enables interconvert. Blank wait uses one payload for request and reply distinguished by direction. Prime and syncobj file exchanges pair a handle with a signed descriptor plus flags and, for timelines, a point. Waits report first signaled only when not waiting for all. Sequence query separates requested identifier from returned active state, sequence and time.

Several records carry user pointers and counts that need validation and safe copying, including DMA lists, context enumeration, syncobj handle and point arrays, and client name bytes. Time appears in mixed widths and splits. Signal based blank wait is marked unsupported, and mode attach and detach are marked deprecated and nonfunctional.

Master is acquired then dropped. Contexts move through add, modify, query, switch, create, remove and result enumeration. Drawables move through add, update and remove. Port memory moves through acquire, enable, alloc, bind, unbind, free and release. Syncobj moves through create, signal, wait, reset, transfer and destroy. Modeset is bracketed by pre and post notifications.

These definitions form the user space interface for direct rendering management, exposing stable structures, flags, event layouts, and numbered ioctl entries that user clients use without seeing kernel internals.
